video_title: Shams Charania on 76ers-Knicks & Kristaps Porzingis considering retirement | The Pat McAfee Show

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on Boston Celtics' early season struggles and adjustments
quotes.excerpt: Boston has a lot that they're still trying to sort through.

text_blocks.speaker: AQ Shipley
text_blocks.text: Do you think it's fair what's happening to Shams right now?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: When you look at yesterday, Boston has a lot that they're still trying to sort through. Jason Tatum took accountability for the tough shooting stretch that he had yesterday in the game. Paul George shot the lights out. We'll see how often he's able to get hot like that moving forward. Boston is going to be better, but I look at inside, Mitchell Robinson at the five position, I don't know how much room for improvement he has. Obviously he said he got his ass kicked on the glass. I think we can swear now, we're on the YouTube side. Javonte Green come off the bench, play well.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: You can say ass anytime, you're an adult.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on Philadelphia 76ers' new roster dynamics and roles
quotes.excerpt: I went into Philadelphia's season thinking, you have five guys that need the ball in their hands.
quotes.quote: I went into Philadelphia's season thinking, you have five guys that need the ball in their hands. Who's going to sacrifice? Where the role is going to be? And clearly, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown from a scoring, from a responsibility perspective, they're going to have it. And then from there, I think LeBron James picking and choosing his spots. He had an almost triple-double. You have Joel Embiid saying after the game he wants to be an all-defensive caliber player. Like that's a mindset shift for him. And then VJ comes in and just does a little bit of everything. I think that's going to be a great game rivalry all season, Philadelphia and New York.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on Oklahoma City Thunder's growth and Chet Holmgren's development
quotes.excerpt: You saw an OKC team that was healthy and Chet Holmgren who was way more aggressive.
quotes.quote: You look at Oklahoma City. I think back to last year, they took San Antonio to seven games because they were down Jalen Williams, they were down AJ Mitchell, and Chet Holmgren by the end of that series. I think he took a total of three shots in that game seven against San Antonio. So, you saw an OKC team that was healthy and Chet Holmgren who was way more aggressive, way more assertive and I think that's what his own health and everyone on that roster's health is going to be very, very key and important.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on Golden State Warriors exploring trades for Kristaps Porzingis
quotes.excerpt: The Warriors are actually already starting to explore trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis.
quotes.quote: There is developing news in the lead up to the NBA season with one of the marquee teams tonight. That's the Golden State Warriors and source tell me that the Warriors are actually already starting to explore trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is out indefinitely as he's dealing with recurring bouts of an autoimmune issue termed as POTS. I'm told he's at the point now where he is seriously contemplating his basketball future and where that could go. The Warriors are down Porzingis, they're down Jimmy Butler, they're down Moses Moody, around Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. That's $90 million in salary that's going to be out for either the significant part of the year or potentially all season.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Shams Charania on Stephen Curry's long-term commitment to the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: Stephen Curry will never be on the move. Stephen Curry will be retiring a Golden State Warrior.
quotes.quote: Stephen Curry will never be on the move. Stephen Curry will be retiring a Golden State Warrior, whether he's playing 19 years, 20 seasons in the NBA, he's going to be there for life. He actually just signed a new contract extension so he's under contract for this season, next season. I think he's got a grand total of three years left on his deal. So, he's good to go moving forward.
